title: SYSK Selects: The 'Satanic Panic' of the 1980s
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of a January 2016 episode on the Satanic Panic of the 1980s, a moral panic in which America widely believed in organized Satanic cults abusing and killing children. The hosts trace roots through religious persecution history, 1970s child abuse awareness and daycare anxieties, and fiction and film, then cover the McMartin and Keller daycare cases, recovered memory therapy and the book Michelle Remembers, the Paul Ingram case, media and talk show complicity, the West Memphis Three and HBO documentaries, the 1994 national survey finding no evidence of Satanic cults, and sociological explanations for the panic. The episode closes with a listener mail segment correcting an earlier remark about Children's Miracle Network balloon donations.

segments.title: Opening and introduction to the Satanic panic
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the Selects episode and the topic, recalling growing up during the Satanic panic and describing it as a moral panic in which Satanic cults were widely believed to be abusing children.

segments.title: Historical roots: persecution and us-versus-them
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how in-group and out-group thinking and Christian theology of good and evil fueled persecutions, including blood libel accusations against Jews and the witch trials, and how art and fiction in the 19th and early 20th centuries built the idea of Satanic cults.

segments.title: Fiction, film and Satanism in popular culture
segments.summary: The hosts cover early Satanic-themed fiction and films such as The Devil Rides Out and Rosemary's Baby, the influence of music and H.P. Lovecraft, and real-life occultists Aleister Crowley and Anton LaVey, and how their imagery drew on earlier myths.

segments.title: 1970s child abuse awareness and daycare anxiety
segments.summary: The hosts describe rising 1970s awareness of child abuse, mandatory reporting laws, the growth in reported cases, and how mothers entering the workforce increased reliance on daycare, fueling parental fear.

segments.title: Keller daycare case in Austin
segments.summary: The hosts describe the accusations against Frances and Dan Keller, who ran a home daycare in Austin, Texas, and how a single child's accusation snowballed into bizarre claims, with bad medical testimony helping sustain the case.

segments.title: Recovered memory therapy and Michelle Remembers
segments.summary: The hosts explain recovered memory therapy, the Keller accuser's therapist involvement, Mike Warnke's fraudulent book, and the 1980 book Michelle Remembers. They note the APA and British bodies' positions and research by Elizabeth Loftus on false memories.

segments.title: Paul Ingram false confession case
segments.summary: The hosts recount the case of Paul Ingram, a sheriff's deputy whose daughter accused him of Satanic ritual abuse, and who confessed despite having no memory of the crimes, serving about twenty years.

segments.title: Media role: talk shows and Geraldo's Satan special
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how talk shows and TV programs, especially Geraldo Rivera's Exposing Satan's Underground special, and children's books and anatomically correct dolls spread the panic for ratings, and how psychology and law enforcement also contributed.
topics: Don't Make Me Go Back Mommy

segments.title: Prosecutions, surveys, exonerations and the end of the panic
segments.summary: The hosts cover the McMartin trial's cost with no convictions, the West Memphis Three and the HBO documentaries Paradise Lost, the Margaret Kelly Michaels exoneration, coercive interview transcripts, and the National Center on Child Abuse and Neglect survey finding no evidence of Satanic cults.

segments.title: Why the panic happened: subversion ideology and rumor panic
segments.summary: The hosts review sociological explanations including subversion ideology, rumor panic, urban legend and millennial anxiety, and reflect on whether other moral panics exist today.

segments.title: Listener mail on Children's Miracle Network balloons
segments.summary: A listener writes that a claim the hosts made about grocery store balloon donations was wrong; the director of Children's Miracle Network Hospitals says corporate partners do not receive tax credits and the hosts say they will look into it.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts thank listeners and point to ways to contact the show.
